notes.title: Enemies finally figured out teamwork
notes.content:
Enemies in Squads[p align="start"]Until now, enemies acted alone, based only on what they themselves knew. Player spotting messages were the only exception. This often led to enemies walking toward player positions with little concern for survival.
[p align="start"]I always wanted the AI to behave more tactically, and I finally had a chance to work on that. To make it both easier for myself and more logical for the game, I grouped all enemies into squads. Individual soldiers no longer make decisions. Instead, squads act as a unit based on commands.
[p align="start"]The system still needs work, but some behaviors are already interesting. If some enemy squad members take heavy damage, the squad pulls back into a defensive position. If they lose too many soldiers, they may retreat entirely. On the offensive side, if one soldier spots a player troop, the rest of the squad moves to support and forms a line of attack.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/5a0d63bb6313543b4976ec5fea4d43c12d38c394.jpg"]Enemy squads moving in spread-out groups toward the player position.


Spotting Mechanics[p align="start"]HUD tracking boxes around ground troops have long been a challenge in gameplay design. On one hand, they are almost necessary for a drone or gunship game since tracking enemies is central to the experience. On the other hand, they can make the game too easy, turning it into a point-and-click exercise. I’ve been working to find a balance where the boxes are not always available.
[p align="start"]I think I now have a system that makes sense and adds to the gameplay. By default, enemy troops are not spotted, so your gunship has no tracking on them. You must zoom in for the auto-detection system to recognize visible enemies and create a track. Zooming out or looking away does not immediately lose the track, but it slowly fades over time. This should incentivize players to zoom in occasionally to assess the situation directly.
[p align="start"]I plan to expand the system so line-of-sight blocking shortens the tracking time. For example, if enemies use smoke or hide in forests, their tracking will be lost faster. Ground troops can also spot enemies for you, refreshing the tracking.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/99a2bf8a22d5e0b4575bfa056f3ba7eace4931cb.jpg"]Enemy tracking box is now red and rotated 45 degrees.


What’s Next[p align="start"]I’ll continue refining squad behaviors and HUD systems. I want to add countermeasures against enemy AA and also start working on the out-of-mission gameplay loop. Resources, research and ammo manufacturing.
[p align="start"]In September I also plan to upload a new build for private playtesting. If you want to take part in it:

Join my mailing list
[p align="start"]What squad setups and sizes would you expect enemies to field?

notes.title: MicroProse Brings New Firepower to Drone Sector
notes.content:
MicroProse is now publishing Drone Sector and providing support that goes far beyond marketing. They are contributing art assets, voice acting and other production work, which allows me to focus on gameplay, features and polish.

I remain the sole developer, but with this extra help I can spend more time creating missions, refining systems and improving the overall experience.


[hr][/hr]

Recent Progress
A lot has changed since the last public news update in May. Here’s a rundown of what’s new and improved:
Enemy Anti-Air Units
• Introduced the first anti-air unit type: surface-to-air missile truck.
• Missiles are fast and highly accurate. Your gunship can survive a few hits, but they can knock out camera feeds or disable weapons.
• Best defense for now: spot and destroy AA before they fire. Proper countermeasures are planned.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/740941037402789d6c19956e218618a4ac0bcf12.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/9072901af95c8f58e1bf287426c533477954b597.jpg"]
AI & Squad Improvements
• Improved squad movement with less clumping and better urban pathing.
• Laid the groundwork for more complex squad commands and improved enemy behaviors.
• Enemies can now find better flanking routes.
• Anti-tank units now fire their rockets.
New Vehicles
• With MicroProse’s help, several new optimized vehicle models have been added, each with modular weapon options.
• Possible loadouts include machine guns, grenade launchers, anti-air guns, autocannons, anti-tank and anti-air rockets, and large-caliber cannons.
• Wheeled vehicle physics are now supported. Previously, only tracked vehicles worked.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/7ef4a7f86ed44d54e34b0b9ac4e15c55ac784dd3.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/5e08c860a77b1c6862b8588407fcd00e6123037d.jpg"]
Improved Radio Chatter
• MicroProse is also assisting with voiceovers, adding far more voice lines than before.
• Radio messages now use a priority system: critical messages play during tense moments, while calmer moments include more ambient chatter.
• Messages are more context-aware.
Visual & Performance Updates
• Improved overall performance on large maps.
• New smoke shell effects block vision for both player and AI, creating new tactical options.
• Upgraded explosion visuals and scorch marks.
• Many buildings can now be destroyed. They burn and prevent enemies from spawning. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/dd02d7a109ac8767bbad8582529c352410f8bf4a.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/c8fdbdb52a0fd2162c06995d90ccc8271469f51d.jpg"]
Code & System Overhaul
• Rebuilt core gameplay systems including gunship movement, weapon firing, projectile flight, damage handling and more. Primarily for improved performance and faster development.
• Removed several third-party plugins that caused issues or slowed progress.
• UI is currently being reworked to improve flexibility and performance. 


[hr][/hr]

The Work Continues
With the new support in place, I’m able to tackle larger parts of the project and work through them at a steady pace. There’s still a lot to build and refine, and I’ll keep sharing progress as it happens.

Follow me on X for smaller day-to-day updates.

notes.title: Drone Sector Demo
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/f116336440214056b5ac95175804c363399d5146.gif
Drone Sector Demo is Here!

The demo includes two missions and several key systems from the main game. Below is a detailed overview of what’s available, along with notes that might help you get the most out of your first run.

Missions
There are two playable missions in the demo. Both of them have some randomization when it comes to enemy positions and objective locations.
Desert Base Map
Smaller (1km x 1km) daytime mission in a relatively narrow canyon valley. Enemies mostly come from one side of the map, making it easier to control them. Be aware that capture objectives might sometimes be on top of the cliffsides, so your ground troops have to make the trek up there.
Swamp Factory Map
Much larger (3km x 3km) nighttime mission in a more urban setting. Lots of streets and industrial buildings providing cover and opportunities for ambush. There is also a small settlement on the other side of the lake from the factory, connected by a bridge. The objectives are spread over a wider area, making it more challenging to keep an eye on everything. There’s no safe corner to back into or single road to block. Enemies can always flank you. Night makes it also harder to see, so make sure to use night or thermal vision.

Objective Types
Capture objective
These can only be completed by ground troops. Your squads have to enter the capture zone and stay within it for about a minute. Capture can only progress if there are not enemies in the zone. Be aware, the capture objective can also take damage and get destroyed which would fail the mission, so don't fire too close to it.
Destroy objective
These are targets you should blow up. They are more durable than enemy troops and often also have an energy shield which regenerates over time. You can destroy it with your guns or by letting the ground squads destroy it by shooting. The latter is slower but uses less of your gunship ammo.
Resource objective (optional)
These are optional capture zones. Ground squads have to stay in them. In demo they don't provide any use, but in the main game there would be a wider variety of resources that can be used for different kinds of weapon upgrades.

Mode System
Your gunship has two modes. Press Tab to switch between them. The UI color changes to help you keep track of which mode you're in.
Command Mode
You can issue move commands to your ground squads. Queue orders with Shift. Troops will choose their own cover and engage enemies independently, but if overwhelmed, they might retreat.
Fire Support Mode
Fire your weapons. Keep in mind that projectiles take time to reach the ground, a few seconds at low altitude, over 10 seconds at high altitude. Always consider movement delay and friendly fire risk. Furthermore, your guns don’t rotate instantly. Wait for the barrels to align with the camera view before firing.

Gunship Weapons

20mm Minigun – Useful against all targets.
40mm Autocannons - A bit more specialized. Sabot rounds are great against armor. Frag rounds are useful against infantry and armor. Airburst rounds are focused on killing infantry.
120mm Cannons - Slower but much more deadly. Airburst rounds kill infantry in a large radius. Direct hits from frag shells can even kill armored targets.
Cluster Bomblets – Perfect for quickly saturating a large area with explosions.
Cluster Landmines – Useful for blocking off roads. Especially ones the enemy armor might use. Keep in mind, that the mines can kill your own troops as well.
150mm Railgun – Extremely fast and deadly. The gun takes longer to aim. Even if it doesn't immediately kill enemy armor, it probably knocks out the crew for a while, making the IFV harmless.
Unguided Rockets – Fast but imprecise. Effective against infantry and can also destroy armor if it happens to land directly on top of it.
Guided Rockets – Extremely fast and precise, always flying towards where you aim. Perfect for responding quickly to mobile enemy IFVs.
Laser – Precise and instant. Good for taking out singular infantry without raising alarm. It can also blind enemy IFVs for a while.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/1d0f774c4e56f81cb3c412537f4f878b4102ba53.gif

Orbit Control

Altitude - High altitude uses less fuel, but shells take longer to reach ground.
Speed - High speed uses more fuel, but allows for faster repositioning.
Orbit Point - You can change what point the gunship orbits around and at what radius.

Enemy Types

Riflemen – Weak alone, dangerous in numbers.
Machine Gunners – They deal more damage.
Grenadiers – Long-range explosive threat.
IFVs – Infantry Fighting Vehicles are a serious threat. Each carries an infantry squad. Just one can kill your whole squad if you aren't careful.

Camera Modes
You can switch between different camera modes. Each mode has its use cases.

Color Vision – Regular camera view. It's usually not as good as other modes, but in certain cases you might have to confirm the color of targets. It's not as important in the demo, but in the final game it will play a more important role.
Night Vision – The usual night vision, brightening up the scenery at the cost of losing color info and also adding noise. On top of that, already bright areas can become overblown with bloom.
Thermal Vision – Great tool for detecting humans and vehicles, as they both are usually warmer than the environment they are in. It does lose detail from the environment though as there are no shadows from the lights and most of the environment is equally warm, making most of the environment appear as a flat gray in thermal vision.

Settings to Know

Speed of Sound – As the game has distance based audio delay, you can control it with this variable. In real life the value is 343 m/s, but for gameplay it can be rather disorienting. Far away explosion sounds can take over 10 seconds to reach you. Higher values make the sound reach you faster and make the gameplay experience smoother, but less realistic.
Night Vision Noise Intensity – Just like real NVGs, Drone Sector night vision has noise. In game it can look really nice, but when recording a video the noise can interfere with video compression and reduce visual quality. If the noise annoys you or you are recording your screen, you might want to turn it down to 0.
Camera Shake Intensity – Heavy gun shots shaking the camera adds to the immersion, but again the shake can get annoying and ruin video recording, in which case it's best to turn it down or off completely.


Private Playtest
If you enjoyed the demo and want to get your hands on the new content earlier, join the private playtest. We are testing new weapons, missions and gameplay systems. Tropical island mission coming soon. Sign up here:
Mailing list
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/fe8d0caa71b51c07454e313726354554761f5cc2.jpg

notes.title: How to Stop a Tank Without Destroying It?
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/ed3df8b9453d70765dd6865a13d716b4089e501c.gif
Physics-Based Vehicles
In the last playtest, vehicles behaved strangely. They could climb over walls or sink into the ground, all because they weren’t using proper physics. That was partly intentional for performance reasons. Now I’ve found a simple but convincing way to give vehicles physics without hurting performance. Wheels have suspension, explosions can push vehicles around, and they can even collide and shove each other.

Squad Order Queue
You can now queue up multiple movement orders for squads. This makes it easier to plan their exact route with the full path displayed on the UI. They’ll follow it step by step until the last waypoint. If plans change, you can quickly cancel everything and set up a new path instead.

Projectile Prediction
Now you can see how long a projectile will take to land, often a few seconds. This works alongside the highlighting system, showing the target’s movement direction and where they’ll be by the time the explosion hits. This makes it much easier to lead shots and land them exactly on a moving target, assuming they don’t change course.

Status Effects on Tanks
Tanks can now be temporarily disabled in different ways. Regular bullets might not do much to the hull, but they can take out optics, blinding the tank for a while. Explosions can break the tracks, immobilizing the vehicle but still leaving it dangerous since the turret can keep firing. The strongest effect comes from certain explosions that concuss the crew, knocking them out temporarily so the tank just sits there until they recover.

Question: What other status effects do you think would be interesting for tanks or infantry, besides blind, immobilize, and stun?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/218231ac2f8ef52b66e834b54717c40131e4755b.gif

notes.title: Splitting the Game in Two (Sort of...)
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/e7b8ac010a5e45e95b0f0f59a7535dffc7f178bb.gif
Mode System
Drone Sector has two core gameplay systems:

 Gunship Combat – This has been the main development focus so far. Based on player feedback, it’s already fun and well-developed.
 Ground Troop Command – Still in early stages. Improving it will be a priority soon.

Combining both systems into a single interface would make controls and UI cluttered. There would be too many overlapping elements competing for space, which isn’t ideal for a game like this. It’s not a slow-paced management sim where heavy UI complexity is acceptable.

To solve this, I split these systems into separate modes. With a quick Tab press, you can switch between:

 Gunship Mode – Focuses on weapons. Displays gun stats, ammo counts, and impact zones. Fewer UI distractions from ground troops.
 Commander Mode – Disables firing and hides the gun info. Displays extra info about squads and objectives. Allows coordinating ground troops. Squads are selected like switching weapons, with different actions for each squad type.

Benefits:

 Keeps both gameplay styles streamlined and intuitive.
 Prevents accidental friendly fire or unintended troop movements.
 Leaves the door open for controller or Steam Deck support.

Localization is Now a Priority
I’ve noticed a surprising amount of Drone Sector’s Steam page traffic is coming from non-English-speaking regions, so I’m prioritizing localization earlier than planned. The first wave of supported languages will include:

 Simplified Chinese
 Japanese
 Korean
 Brazilian Portuguese
 German
 French
 Italian
 Spanish

Localization comes with challenges—adjusting UI for different text sizes, optimizing font rendering, and ensuring smooth performance—but progress is steady. If there’s a language you’d like to see, let me know in the comments!

notes.title: One Week of Private Playtesting
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/afcd91a4a987f457e68b319754c19527ec2c4986.gif
Successful Playtest
Last week I ran a private playtest with my mailing list followers. Everything went really smoothly, so I'm happy.

 Over 100 players tried out the game
 Players got to try 2 different maps and 13 different weapons
 More than 80 total hours of play time
 100+ successful missions
 300+ failed missions

Most Common Requests

 Soldier Radio Chatter: Many players want more immersion with radio calls from on-the-ground soldiers. I completely agree — it makes the battlefield feel more tactical and also helps the gameplay. I’m already planning to bring in voice actors.
 Clearer Objectives: Many players mentioned it can be unclear what to do during mission. I plan to add more detailed mission prompts and UI elements to address this, with a comprehensive tutorial coming later in development.

Interesting Data

 The smaller desert base map is well-liked.
 The bigger swamp factory night map is more polarizing: some love it, some find it less appealing.
 Everyone loves the minigun!
 Railgun and rockets are popular.
 40mm autocannons get mixed reactions; 120mm cannons are clearly underpowered.
 The laser is currently the weakest option.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/ccec0e306803311c448713bb5ddd2ed3087f1dd6.gif

notes.title: Introducing the Latest in Tactical Firepower
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/59aa1c691b2f81d4c2220a6f71879236dbb9567c.gif
Expanding the Arsenal
Minigun: A rapid-fire weapon perfect for shredding through infantry with devastating efficiency.

Autocannons: A versatile weapon system with multiple ammo types:

Airburst Rounds: Explodes above ground, scattering fragments in a concentrated cone—ideal for densely packed infantry.

Fragmentation Rounds: Creates a spherical explosion on impact, covering a wider area but with less concentrated damage.

APFSDS (armor-piercing, fin-stabilized, discarding sabot) Rounds: Specialized for piercing heavy armor with pinpoint precision. Best against vehicles and fortified targets.

Railgun: A cutting-edge weapon with unparalleled muzzle velocity and devastating firepower. Though slower to reload and expensive to operate, its precision and speed make it ideal for neutralizing vehicles before they can react.

Radiation Laser: Delivers instant damage with exceptional accuracy, making it a surgical tool for high-value infantry targets. However, its power is ineffective against armored vehicles, as they can deflect the laser entirely.

Cluster Munitions: Devastating area-of-effect weapons that unleash smaller explosives:

AP (anti-personnel) Minefield: Mines detonate on contact, posing a serious danger to anyone who moves carelessly—enemy or ally alike. The explosions can create chaos among enemies, with panicked troops accidentally triggering additional mines in a chain reaction.

Fragmentation Bomblets: Impact grenades that cover an extremely wide area, making it nearly impossible for infantry to escape. This devastating weapon is highly effective but also poses significant risks, as its indiscriminate blasts can easily harm allies or civilians caught in the area.

Light Flare Shell: Detonates high above the ground, deploying a brightly glowing flare to illuminate the battlefield. While less common in modern operations, it serves as a fallback for visibility during night missions when thermal or night vision systems aren’t available.

Enhanced Combat Systems
I’ve refined many aspects of how gunship weapons work for a more immersive experience:

Enhanced Audio and Visual Effects: Weapons now sound and feel more impactful, with detailed effects and optimized performance.

Recoil and Gunship Shake: Every weapon now causes the gunship to shake based on its size and power. Heavier weapons produce stronger recoil, but camera zoom adjustments ensure this doesn’t interfere with precision targeting.

Gun Turn Speed: Weapons now have realistic turn rates, adding a layer of tactical planning. Heavier weapons can take several seconds to align, rewarding players who anticipate and position wisely.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/6c4f0fe601f0cd735772ee4b6b2b6dc9d86c1e5e.gif
Want to see these weapons in action?
Check out my YouTube channel for quick clips showcasing these latest systems!

notes.title: Two Weeks After Launch: What’s Next?
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289376/5bd2a649b8f05690bc1fb336cb2f1c4fd7d23e5e.gif

Two Weeks Since the Announcement
The announcement week was a rush, but it went better than I expected! A lot of you seem excited about Drone Sector - we’ve already surpassed 400+ wishlists. Thanks for following along!

Looking Ahead: The Next Milestone
As part of the development roadmap, I’m planning to kick off private playtesting early next year, potentially as soon as January. The focus for this first round will be on gathering feedback about the core gameplay loop: engaging ground targets while keeping your own ground troops alive.

Initially, the demo will feature one level with a handful of enemy types. Over time, I hope to expand testing with additional levels and mission types.

If you’d like to be part of this early testing group, sign up for my mailing list! Participants for the first demo will be selected exclusively from the list.
